import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Vaught conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaught_conjecture)
-/

namespace VaughtConjecture

open FirstOrder.Language

/-- The number of countable models of some L-Theory T up to isomorphism -/
def numberOfCountableModels {L : FirstOrder.Language} (T : L.Theory) : Cardinal :=
  Cardinal.mk (Quotient (Setoid.comap
    (fun (model : {mt : T.ModelType // Countable mt.Carrier}) ↦
    CategoryTheory.Bundled.mk model.val.Carrier model.val.struc)
    equivSetoid))

/--
The Vaught conjecture states that for a countable language L and a complete L-Theory T
the number of countable models of T (up to isomorphism) is finite, $\aleph_0$ or $2^{\aleph_0}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem vaught_conjecture {L : FirstOrder.Language} (hL : Countable L.Symbols)
                          {T : L.Theory} (hT : T.IsComplete) :
  numberOfCountableModels T ≤ Cardinal.aleph0 ∨ numberOfCountableModels T = Cardinal.continuum
  := by sorry

end VaughtConjecture

reformulations.difference: Lean counts all at-most-countable models, including finite models, and does not require T to have an infinite model. The source’s detailed formulation assumes an infinite model and uses I(T, ℵ₀), counting only countably infinite models.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If a complete T has an infinite model, completeness forces every model to be infinite, so the Lean count equals I(T, ℵ₀). If T has a finite model M, completeness forces every model to have the same finite cardinality and to be isomorphic to M. This holds even for an infinite language: nonisomorphism between finite structures is witnessed by a finite reduct and distinguished by a sentence. Thus the Lean count is 1 in the additional cases, making the first disjunct automatic. The finite-model convention therefore changes neither the problem nor its answer. Also, c ≤ ℵ₀ means precisely that c is finite or equals ℵ₀; the usual upper bound of continuum for countable-language countable models makes the stated disjunction equivalent to the source’s prohibition on ℵ₀ < I(T, ℵ₀) < continuum.

review.notes: Both declarations were checked. ModelType already excludes empty carriers, IsComplete includes satisfiability, and equivSetoid uses genuine structure isomorphism rather than elementary equivalence. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles and proves universe invariance of the count, equivalence of the independently inferred universes in the two disjuncts, the cardinal rewrites, infinitude transfer for complete theories, and boundary checks: unsatisfiable theories have count 0, while the singleton theory and the theory of an infinite pure set each have count 1. These proofs do not depend on sorryAx. The full finite-model reformulation was checked mathematically, not proved as a complete Lean equivalence. The cited source explicitly describes Knight’s counterexample as unverified, consistent with research open. The reviewed file remains identical to the committed version.
